title: Sam Altman: Jensen Huang “Selling Picks and Shovels” as NVIDIA Heads for $6 Trillion
key_facts: Nvidia hit a record high this week, with a market value of about $5.8 trillion.
Vanity Fair's Mark Guiducci made the 'picks and shovels' remark about Huang to Altman on the Fair Game podcast.
Altman declined to play along: 'First of all, I never think this way.'
Analysts expect Nvidia's earnings per share to roughly double this fiscal year; the stock trades near 20 times forward earnings, about half its five-year average.
OpenAI plans to start deploying its first custom chip, made with Broadcom, by the end of this year.
Nvidia authorised another $150 billion in share buybacks.
quote_evidence: "I think Jensen Huang will be the guy who was selling picks and shovels during the gold rush."
Altman declined to play along: "First of all, I never think this way."
why_it_matters_hint: An investor column argues Nvidia's valuation looks modest next to its earnings growth.
notes: Yahoo Finance page appears to carry a TIKR-sponsored opinion piece; the original author is not named. The 'picks and shovels' line is Guiducci's, not Altman's. Analyst numbers (earnings, multiples) are as cited by the column, not checked.
